source.title: Indecomposable vector bundles and stable Higgs bundles over smooth projective curves
source.read: arXiv v2 (4 October 2014), the last preprint version, whose comment records that corollaries on the number of irreducible components of the stable global nilpotent cone were added; these are Corollaries 1.9 and 1.10 below. Read in the LaTeX source of that version (arXiv e-print of 1406.3839v2, file Indecomposables.tex, 2143 lines, sha256 of the source archive a84104fa77de6dc5731dac7add9c97badafe9e33793daa78c7d03048ffa40467), fetched 22 September 2026. The published version in the Annals of Mathematics could not be read here: the article page and its PDF are reachable but no PDF text extraction is available in this environment, so every locator below is a preprint locator and the four source issues are recorded against the preprint with no claim about print. The preprint numbers Theorems, Lemmas, Corollaries, Propositions and Conjectures by a single counter per section, so that Theorem 1.1, Theorem 1.2, Conjecture 1.3, Conjecture 1.4, Theorem 1.5, Corollary 1.6 and so on run consecutively; the four theorems called Theorem 1, 2, 3 and 4 in the text are Theorems 1.1, 1.2, 1.5 and 7.1. Definitions are not numbered and are made in running text inside numbered paragraphs such as 1.1, 2.2, 6.4; those paragraph numbers are used as locators for the definitional items below.
readSections: 1 Introduction (1.1 Weil numbers and the ring K_g, 1.2 the counting functions and Theorem 1, 1.3 the explicit formula and Theorem 2 with Conjectures 1.3 and 1.4, 1.4 stable Higgs bundles, Theorem 3 and its corollaries, 1.5 plan)
2 Orbifolds of pairs (2.1 classes, the Euler form and the Harder–Narasimhan categories, 2.2 the groupoids of nilpotent pairs and their volume)
3 Jordan stratification (3.1 Jordan types and the groupoids of filtered sheaves, 3.2 the functors π, π′, π″ and the volumes of their fibres)

4 Hall algebras of curves (4.1 the Hall algebra, 4.2 characteristic functions and volumes, 4.3 Eisenstein series, 4.4 truncations, 4.5 the spherical Hall algebra and its generic form, 4.6 Zariski density)
5 Volume of the orbifold of pairs (5.1–5.8: the generating series, the shuffle formulas and the proof of Theorem 2)

6 Relation to the number of points of Hitchin moduli spaces (6.1–6.11: Higgs bundles, quot schemes, the Kronecker quiver presentation, GIT, the deformation and the proof of Theorem 3, then Corollaries 1.6–1.10)
Appendix A Volume of moduli stacks of torsion sheaves
Appendix B Density of Weil numbers of smooth projective curves
Appendix C Proof of Conjecture 1.3 when r is prime

summary: Schiffmann proves that the number of geometrically indecomposable vector bundles of rank r and degree d on a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X of genus g over a finite field is given by a universal function of the Weil numbers of X, computes that function explicitly, and identifies it with the point count of the moduli space of stable Higgs bundles. Precisely: there is a unique A_{g,r,d} in the localization K_g of Q[T_g]^{W_g} with A_{r,d}(X) = A_{g,r,d}(σ_X) for every such curve, where T_g is the torus of tuples (α_1,…,α_{2g}) with α_{2i−1}α_{2i} constant and σ_X the class of the Weil numbers; A_{g,r,d} is computed by an explicit residue formula from a plethystic logarithm of a sum over partitions of products J_λ(z)H_λ(z), where J_λ is a product of zeta values over the boxes of the Young diagram and H_λ an iterated residue of a symmetrising kernel; and when (r,d) are coprime and the characteristic exceeds an explicit bound, |Higgs^st_{r,d}(X)(F_q)| = q^{1+(g−1)r²}A_{r,d}(X). The proof has two halves. The arithmetic half counts pairs (F,θ) with θ a nilpotent endomorphism: their groupoid volume is the plethystic exponential of the counting series, by Krull–Schmidt, and the volume is computed by stratifying according to the Jordan type of θ and evaluating the fibres of the resulting functors, which turns the problem into a pairing of Eisenstein series in the Hall algebra of the curve; the spherical Hall algebra has a generic form over Q[T_g]^{W_g}, which makes every volume a function of σ_X alone, and Zariski density of the Weil numbers of genus-g curves gives uniqueness. The geometric half transports Crawley-Boevey and Van den Bergh's quiver argument to curves: the stack of Higgs bundles is presented by a quot scheme built from two line bundles and embedded in the representation space of a Kronecker quiver, indecomposability becomes a condition on the image of the moment map, and a smooth family over the affine line has the stable Higgs moduli space as its special fibre and the indecomposable bundles over the others; a contracting G_m-action and the Bialynicki-Birula–Hesselink decomposition make the point counts agree. The consequences are the purity of the cohomology of Higgs^st_{r,d}, its Poincaré polynomial over F_q and over C, and the count of the irreducible components of the stable global nilpotent cone as A_{g,r,d}(0); the extensions are the parabolic case and a group of conjectures, including that A_{g,r,d} is independent of d and a curve analogue of Kac's conjecture. The atlas has the two ends of this story and neither of its middles: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.0 constructs Bun_G on a global curve with its Harder–Narasimhan bounded opens, EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.2b the Hitchin base and map for a reductive group over a curve over a finite field, AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.2 the Quot schemes, FunctionFieldArithmetic the curve, its adeles and its zeta function, DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.0 the Weil numbers, and the Tau Ceti roadmap on quiver representations the local model — Krull–Schmidt, the Euler form, Auslander–Reiten theory — for what this paper does globally. Nothing plans Hall algebras in any form, nor Eisenstein series in Hall-algebra form, nor counting problems for bundles, nor Kac polynomials, nor GIT for quiver representations. Of the 59 items, one is in Mathlib (Young diagrams and partitions), three are planned, and the remaining 55 are routed: 51 to a new roadmap, and four as sources of GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.0, DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.0 and EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.2b.

items.name: Weil numbers, the torus T_g and the ring K_g
items.statement: Let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g over F_q and let σ_1, …, σ_{2g} be its Weil numbers, the eigenvalues of Frobenius on H^1(X ⊗ F̄_q, Q̄_l) for a prime l ∤ q, so that ζ_X(z) = ∏_{i=1}^{2g}(1 − σ_i z)/((1−z)(1−qz)). Under an embedding ι : Q̄_l → C they satisfy σ̄_{2i−1} = σ_{2i} and σ_{2i−1}σ_{2i} = q. Set T_g = {(α_1, …, α_{2g}) ∈ G_m^{2g} : α_{2i−1}α_{2i} = α_{2j−1}α_{2j} for all i, j}, on which W_g = S_g ⋉ (S_2)^g acts, so that {σ_1, …, σ_{2g}} defines a canonical element σ_X ∈ T_g(C)/W_g. Write q also for the element α_{2i−1}α_{2i} ∈ Q[T_g]^{W_g}, put R_g = Q[T_g]^{W_g}, and let K_g be the localization of R_g at the multiplicative set generated by {q^l − 1 : l ≥ 1}.
items.note: The ring in which all the counting polynomials of the paper live. DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.0 defines Weil q-numbers and their weights and FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.5 identifies the curve zeta function and its numerator, so the Weil numbers themselves are planned; the torus T_g with its W_g-action, the invariant ring R_g and its localization K_g, and the point σ_X ∈ T_g/W_g attached to a curve, are not.

items.name: The counting functions A_{r,d}(X)
items.statement: For r > 0 and d ∈ Z let A_{r,d}(X) denote the number of geometrically indecomposable vector bundles on X of rank r and degree d, that is vector bundles V such that V ⊗_{F_q} F̄_q is indecomposable. More generally, for α = (r,d) ∈ (Z²)^+ let A_α(X) be the number of geometrically indecomposable coherent sheaves of class α, and A_α^{≥0}(X) the number of those lying in C_{≥0}. These numbers are finite, by the existence of Harder–Narasimhan filtrations.
items.note: The quantity the paper computes. GS.0 constructs Bun_G with its Harder–Narasimhan bounded opens and the finiteness of the relevant bounded opens, which is what makes these counts finite; the counts themselves, and the notion of a geometrically indecomposable bundle, are planned nowhere.

items.name: Theorem 1: polynomiality of the count of indecomposable bundles
items.statement: For any fixed genus g and any pair (r,d) ∈ N × Z there is a unique element A_{g,r,d} ∈ K_g such that A_{r,d}(X) = A_{g,r,d}(σ_X) for every smooth projective geometrically connected curve X of genus g defined over a finite field. Conjecturally A_{g,r,d} lies in Q[T_g]^{W_g}, so that no localization is needed.
items.note: The first main theorem, a global analogue of Kac's theorem that the number of geometrically indecomposable representations of a quiver over F_q is a polynomial in q. Nothing in the atlas plans it; the Tau Ceti roadmap on quiver representations plans the Krull–Schmidt and Gabriel theory but not Kac's counting theorem.

items.name: Partitions, arms, legs and the pairing ⟨λ, μ⟩
items.statement: For a partition λ = (λ_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ λ_l > 0) the Young diagram is the set of boxes (i,j) with 1 ≤ i ≤ λ_j; for a box s ∈ λ, a(s) is the armlength, the number of boxes strictly to the right of s, and l(s) the leglength, the number strictly above. For partitions λ, μ one sets ⟨λ, μ⟩ = Σ_i λ′_i μ′_i, where λ′, μ′ are the conjugate partitions.
items.note: Mathlib has YoungDiagram with its cells, rowLen, colLen and transpose (the conjugate partition), and Nat.Partition; armlength and leglength are rowLen and colLen of the diagram measured from a box, and ⟨λ,μ⟩ is the sum of the products of the transposed row lengths.

items.name: Plethystic exponential and logarithm
items.statement: On K_g[[z,T]] define for l ≥ 1 the l-th Adams operator ψ_l as the Q-algebra map with α_i ↦ α_i^l, z ↦ z^l, T ↦ T^l. With K_g[[z,T]]^+ = zK_g[[z,T]] + TK_g[[z,T]], the plethystic exponential and logarithm are mutually inverse maps Exp : K_g[[z,T]]^+ → 1 + K_g[[z,T]]^+ and Log : 1 + K_g[[z,T]]^+ → K_g[[z,T]]^+ given by Exp(f) = exp(Σ_k ψ_k(f)/k) and Log(f) = Σ_{k≥1} (μ(k)/k) ψ_k(log f). They satisfy Exp(f+g) = Exp(f)Exp(g) and Log(fg) = Log(f) + Log(g), and Exp(z) = 1/(1−z). One sets ζ(z) = Exp((1 − Σ_i α_i + q)z) = ∏_i(1 − α_i z)/((1−z)(1−qz)) and ζ̃(z) = z^{1−g}ζ(z), so that ζ_X(z) = ζ(z)(σ_X).
items.note: The λ-ring formalism in which all the generating series are written. Mathlib has the Möbius function (ArithmeticFunction.moebius) and power sums (MvPolynomial.psum) but no λ-ring or Adams operations, and no layer of the atlas plans plethystic operators.

items.name: The rational functions J_λ(z), L(z_n,…,z_1) and H_λ(z)
items.statement: For a partition λ = (1^{r_1}2^{r_2}⋯t^{r_t}) set J_λ(z) = ∏_{s∈λ} ζ*_X(q^{−1−l(s)}z^{a(s)}), where ζ*_X(q^{−u}z^v) = ζ_X(q^{−u}z^v) unless (u,v) = (1,0), in which case it is ∏_i(1−α_i^{−1})/(1−q^{−1}). With n = l(λ) = Σ_i r_i and r_{<i}, r_{>i}, r_{[i,j]} the partial sums, put L(z_n,…,z_1) = (∏_{i<j} ζ̃(z_i/z_j))^{−1} Σ_{σ∈S_n} σ{∏_{i<j} ζ̃(z_i/z_j) · ∏_{i<n}(1 − q z_{i+1}/z_i)^{−1} · (1−z_1)^{−1}}. Let Res_λ be the iterated residue along z_{k+1}/z_k = q^{−1} within each block of λ. Set H̃_λ(z_{1+r_{<t}}, …, z_1) = Res_λ[L(z_n,…,z_1) ∏_{j ∉ {r_{≤i}}} dz_j/z_j] and H_λ(z) = H̃_λ(z^t q^{−r_{<t}}, …, z^i q^{−r_{<i}}, …, z).
items.note: The combinatorial ingredients of the explicit formula. They are built from the zeta function of the curve and an iterated residue of a symmetrising kernel of Macdonald type; nothing comparable is planned in the atlas.

items.name: Theorem 2: the explicit formula for A_{g,r,d}
items.statement: Define rational functions A_{g,r}(z) ∈ K_g(z) by Σ_{r≥1} A_{g,r}(z)T^r = (q−1)·Log(Σ_λ q^{(g−1)⟨λ,λ⟩} J_λ(z) H_λ(z) T^{|λ|}). Then for every d ∈ Z, A_{g,r,d} = −Σ_{ξ ∈ μ_r} ξ^{−d} Res_{z=ξ}(A_{g,r}(z) dz/z), where μ_r is the set of r-th roots of unity. For r ≤ 2 one has A_{g,1,d} = ∏_{i=1}^{2g}(1−α_i) and an explicit closed formula for A_{g,2,d}.
items.note: The second main theorem, which makes the first effective. It is closely parallel to the Hausel–Rodriguez-Villegas conjectural formula for the mixed Hodge polynomial of the character variety and to Mozgovoy's extension, differing by the factors H_λ(z).

items.name: Conjecture 1: independence of the degree
items.statement: The polynomial A_{g,r,d} does not depend on d. Equivalently, by Theorem 2, the rational function A_{g,r}(z) is regular at the nontrivial r-th roots of unity; since A_{g,r}(z) is regular outside μ_r with at most simple poles, this says (1−z)A_{g,r}(z) ∈ K_g[z], in which case A_{g,r,d} = [(1−z)A_{g,r}(z)]_{z=1} for all d. The conjecture is proved by direct computation when r is prime.
items.locator: arXiv:1406.3839v2 (4 October 2014), Conjectures 1.3 and 1.4, proved for r prime in Appendix C
items.note: Stated as Conjectures 1.3 and 1.4 and proved for r prime in Appendix C; by Theorem 2 it is essentially equivalent to a conjecture of Hausel and Thaddeus that the motive of Higgs^st_{r,d} is independent of d. It is a conjecture, not a theorem, and must be recorded as such.

items.name: Stable Higgs bundles and their moduli space
items.statement: Let Ω_X be the canonical bundle. A Higgs sheaf of rank r and degree d is a pair (V, θ) with V coherent of rank r and degree d and θ ∈ Hom(V, V ⊗ Ω_X). A Higgs subsheaf is a subsheaf W ⊆ V with θ(W) ⊆ W ⊗ Ω_X; (V,θ) is semistable (resp. stable) if μ(W) ≤ μ(V) (resp. <) for every proper Higgs subsheaf, and a Higgs subsheaf with μ(W) > μ(V) is destabilizing. For r > 0 a semistable Higgs sheaf is a Higgs bundle. Higgs_{r,d}(X) and Coh_{r,d}(X) are the moduli stacks of Higgs sheaves and of coherent sheaves, algebraic over k, locally of finite type, of dimensions 2(g−1)r² and (g−1)r². For (r,d) coprime, Higgs^st_{r,d}(X) is the open substack of stable Higgs bundles, represented by a smooth connected k-scheme. By Serre duality Higgs_{r,d}(X) also parametrises pairs (V, ν) with ν ∈ Ext^1(V,V)^*, a Higgs subsheaf being a subsheaf W with a(ν) ∈ b(Ext^1(W,W)^*) for the canonical maps a, b.
items.note: EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.2b constructs, for a smooth proper curve over a finite field and a reductive group scheme in good characteristic, the stack of G-bundles, Higgs fields twisted by a chosen sufficiently positive divisor, the Hitchin base and map, and the Picard stack acting on Hitchin fibres; GS.0 constructs Bun_G. The case needed here is GL_r with the canonical twist and the stable locus for coprime (r,d), and the Serre-duality description by pairs (V,ν) is the paper's own reformulation.

items.name: Theorem 3: counting points of the stable Higgs moduli space
items.statement: Let (r,d) be relatively prime. There is an explicit constant C = C(r,d) such that for every smooth projective geometrically connected curve X of genus g over F_q with char(F_q) > C one has |Higgs^st_{r,d}(X)(F_q)| = q^{1+(g−1)r²} · A_{r,d}(X).
items.note: The third main theorem: the number of stable Higgs bundles is the number of indecomposable bundles, up to the factor q^{1+(g−1)r²} = q^{dim}/2 … more precisely q^{1−⟨α,α⟩}. Its proof, inspired by Crawley-Boevey and Van den Bergh for quivers, occupies Section 6. A companion paper with Mozgovoy proves it in all characteristics.

items.name: Purity and the Poincaré polynomial of the Higgs moduli space
items.statement: Let (r,d) be relatively prime. Then A_{g,r,d} ∈ N[−z_1, …, −z_{2g}]^{W_g}, and for every smooth geometrically connected projective curve X of genus g over F_q with p > C(r,d) the Frobenius eigenvalues on H^n_c(Higgs^st_{r,d}(X ⊗ F̄_q), Q̄_l) are of the form ∏_j σ_j^{n_j} with Σ n_j = n, the multiplicity of σ_1^{i_1}⋯σ_{2g}^{i_{2g}} being the coefficient a_{i_1,…,i_{2g}} of A_{g,r,d} written in the variables (−z_j). In particular Σ_n dim H_c^n(Higgs^st_{r,d}(X̄), Q̄_l) t^n = t^{2(1+(g−1)r²)} A_{g,r,d}(t,…,t), and the same formula holds with singular compactly supported cohomology for a compact Riemann surface X_C of genus g. Consequently A_{g,r,d} is unitary of degree 2(1+(g−1)r²).
items.note: Corollaries 1.6, 1.7 and 1.8. They combine Theorems 1–3 with the purity of the cohomology of Higgs^st_{r,d} and the comparison between the finite-field and complex cases; without the coprimality assumption they would give a global analogue of Kac's positivity conjecture for quivers, which is what Conjecture 1 would supply.

items.name: The stable global nilpotent cone
items.statement: Let μ : Higgs^st_{r,d} → A be the Hitchin map and Λ^st_{r,d} its zero fibre, the stable global nilpotent cone, a projective and in general singular Lagrangian subvariety of Higgs^st_{r,d}. Assume gcd(r,d) = 1. Then (i) over F_q, Λ^st_{r,d} is cohomologically pure, the Frobenius eigenvalues on H^i(Λ^st_{r,d}, Q̄_l) are of the form ∏_j α_j^{l_j} with Σ l_j = i, and |Λ^st_{r,d}(F_q)| = Ā_{g,r,d}(σ_X) where Ā_{g,r,d}(z) = q^{2(1+(g−1)r²)}A_{g,r,d}(z^{−1}) is the Poincaré dual of A_{g,r,d}; (ii) over F_q or C, dim H^{1+(g−1)r²}(Λ^st_{r,d}, C) = dim H^{1+(g−1)r²}(Higgs^st_{r,d}, C) = A_{g,r,d}(0), so that the number of irreducible components of Λ^st_{r,d} is A_{g,r,d}(0).
items.note: Corollary 1.9, added in v2. ET.2b constructs the Hitchin base and map for a reductive group and the Picard stack acting on the fibres, but not the nilpotent cone, its purity, or the count of its irreducible components.

items.name: A generating series for the constant terms A_{g,r,d}(0)
items.statement: Define A^0_{g,r}(z) by Σ_r A^0_{g,r}(z)T^r = −Log(Σ_λ z^{(g−1)⟨λ,λ⟩−l(λ)} K_λ(z) T^{|λ|}) where, for λ = (1^{r_1}2^{r_2}⋯), K_λ(z) = 1/∏_i ∏_{j=1}^{r_i}(1 − z^{−j}). Then A_{g,r,d}(0) = Σ_{ξ∈μ_r} ξ^{−d} Res_{z=ξ}(A^0_{g,r}(z) dz/z). For r ≤ 4 one has A_{g,1,d}(0) = 1, A_{g,2,d}(0) = C(g,1), A_{g,3,d}(0) = 4C(g,2) + C(g,1) and A_{g,4,d}(0) = 32C(g,3) + 20C(g,2) + C(g,1); for every r, A_{g,r,d}(0) is a polynomial in g of degree r − 1.
items.note: Corollary 1.10. The formula differs from Hua's formula for the Kac polynomial of the g-loop quiver only by the extra term −l(λ), and A_{g,r,d}(0) is conjecturally equal to A_{Σ_g,r}(1).

items.name: Classes, the Euler form and the Harder–Narasimhan categories
items.statement: For a coherent sheaf F on X put [F] = (rank F, deg F) ∈ (Z²)^+ = {(r,d) ∈ N × Z : d > 0 if r = 0}. The Euler form on K_0(Coh X), ⟨F,G⟩ = dim Hom(F,G) − dim Ext^1(F,G), depends only on the classes and is ⟨(r,d),(r′,d′)⟩ = (1−g)rr′ + (rd′ − r′d); (α,β) denotes its symmetrisation. With the slope μ(F) = deg F/rank F, C_ν is the subcategory of semistable sheaves of slope ν; for α_1, …, α_t with μ(α_1) > ⋯ > μ(α_t), C_{α_1,…,α_t} ⊆ Coh_{Σα_i}(X) consists of the sheaves whose Harder–Narasimhan filtration has subquotients of classes α_i, and it contains finitely many isomorphism classes. C_{≥ν} consists of the sheaves whose Harder–Narasimhan slopes are all ≥ ν, and C_{≤ν} similarly. C_{≥0} is stable under quotients and extensions, contains finitely many isomorphism classes in each class α, and is preserved by extension of the base field; D(α) = {(α_1,…,α_t) : α = Σα_i, μ(α_1) > ⋯ > μ(α_t) ≥ 0} is finite.
items.note: GS.0 constructs Bun_G with its Harder–Narasimhan bounded opens, proves that the relevant bounded opens are of finite type and accounts for automorphisms and central degree; the Euler form of a curve and the slope stratification are part of that package. The Tau Ceti quiver roadmap plans the Euler and Tits forms in the quiver setting, which is the model for this one.

items.name: Krull–Schmidt for coherent sheaves on a curve
items.statement: (i) Coh(X) is a Krull–Schmidt category: every coherent sheaf M decomposes as M = M_1^{⊕n_1} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ M_s^{⊕n_s} with the M_i distinct indecomposables, and the pairs (M_i, n_i) are unique up to permutation. (ii) If M is indecomposable then k_M := End(M)/rad(End(M)) is a field. (iii) If M, M′ are distinct indecomposables then any composite M → M′ → M lies in rad(End(M)).
items.note: The Tau Ceti roadmap on quiver representations builds Fitting's lemma, the local-endomorphism-ring criterion and the Krull–Schmidt theorem for finite-length modules over a finite-dimensional algebra, and records that Mathlib has neither. Coherent sheaves on a projective curve are not modules over a finite-dimensional algebra, so the statement needed here — Krull–Schmidt for a Hom-finite category with local endomorphism rings of indecomposables, which is Atiyah's theorem of 1956 — is not covered. A reviewer may prefer a Part II of that Tau Ceti roadmap for the general Krull–Schmidt-category statement rather than a fresh treatment inside the new roadmap.

items.name: The radical of the endomorphism algebra of a decomposition
items.statement: Let M_1, …, M_s be distinct indecomposables, n_1, …, n_s ∈ N and M = ⊕_i M_i^{⊕n_i}. Then rad(End M) = ⊕_{i≠j} Hom(M_i^{⊕n_i}, M_j^{⊕n_j}) ⊕ ⊕_i rad(End M_i)^{⊕n_i}, and End(M)/rad(End M) ≅ ∏_i gl(n_i, k_{M_i}) is semisimple.
items.note: The computation of the radical, from which the volume formula of the next item follows.

items.name: Nilpotent endomorphisms against automorphisms
items.statement: With M as above, |End^{nil}(M)|/|Aut(M)| = ∏_i |k_{M_i}|^{n_i(n_i−1)}/|GL(n_i, k_{M_i})|, where End^{nil} denotes the nilpotent endomorphisms. This uses that End^{nil}(M) and Aut(M) are the preimages under End(M) → ∏_i gl(n_i, k_{M_i}) of the product of nilpotent cones, resp. of the product of general linear groups, together with |N_{n,k}| = |k|^{n(n−1)}.
items.note: The local computation that turns a count of pairs (F, θ) into a count of indecomposables; the cardinality of the nilpotent cone of gl_n over a finite field is the only external input, and it is not in the libraries.

items.name: The groupoids of nilpotent pairs and their volume
items.statement: For a coherent sheaf F let End^{nil}(F) be the space of nilpotent endomorphisms. Nil_α(X) is the groupoid of pairs (F, θ) with F ∈ Coh_α(X) and θ ∈ End^{nil}(F), an isomorphism (F,θ) → (G,φ) being an isomorphism j : F → G with jθ = φj. For rk(α) > 0 this groupoid has infinite volume; the full subgroupoid Nil_α^{≥0}(X) of pairs with F ∈ C_{≥0} has finite volume vol(Nil_α^{≥0}(X)) = Σ_{F ∈ Coh^{≥0}_α(X)/≅} |End^{nil}(F)|/|Aut(F)| and is empty when deg α < 0.
items.note: The orbifold of pairs whose volume is the paper's main computational object; nothing in the atlas plans groupoid volumes of moduli of sheaves with a nilpotent endomorphism.

items.name: Volume of the orbifold of pairs as a plethystic exponential
items.statement: In Q[[z^{(1,0)}, z^{(0,1)}]] one has Σ_α vol(Nil_α^{≥0}(X)) z^α = exp(Σ_{l≥1} (1/l) Σ_α (A_α^{≥0}(X ⊗ F_{q^l})/(q^l − 1)) z^{lα}), or loosely Σ_α vol(Nil_α^{≥0}(X)) z^α = Exp(Σ_α (A_α^{≥0}(X)/(q−1)) z^α). The proof uses Krull–Schmidt, the previous volume formula, Heine's formula Σ_{n≥0} u^n/((1−v^n)⋯(1−v)) = exp(Σ_{l≥1} u^l/(l(1−v^l))), and the Galois-orbit count relating indecomposables over F_q and over its extensions.
items.note: Proposition 2.1: the bridge between the volume of the orbifold of pairs and the counting functions. It is the exact analogue of the corresponding step in Kac's and Hua's work for quivers.

items.name: Large degree forces the Harder–Narasimhan slopes to be non-negative
items.statement: Assume d > (g−1)r(r−1). Then every indecomposable vector bundle of rank r and degree d lies in C_{≥0}, so that A_{r,d}^{≥0}(X) = A_{r,d}(X). The proof uses that a short exact sequence 0 → A → B → C → 0 with A ∈ C_{≥ν}, C ∈ C_{≤ν′} and ν − ν′ > 2g − 2 splits, by Serre duality.
items.note: Proposition 2.5, which lets the truncated count be replaced by the honest one in a range and hence, with the previous item, computes A_{r,d}(X).

items.name: The Jordan type of a nilpotent pair and its stratification
items.statement: For (F, θ) ∈ Nil_α(X) with θ^s = 0 and θ^{s−1} ≠ 0, the Jordan type is J(F,θ) = (α_1, …, α_s) defined by [Ker θ^i] − [Ker θ^{i−1}] = α_i + α_{i+1} + ⋯ + α_s for i = 1, …, s; then Σ_i i α_i = α, some α_i may vanish but α_s ≠ 0. The generic Jordan type is J^gen(F,θ) = (rk α_1, …, rk α_t) with t largest with rk α_t ≠ 0. Writing Nil_{α̲}(X) for the groupoid of pairs of Jordan type α̲ gives a stratification Nil_α(X) = ⊔_{|α̲| = α} Nil_{α̲}(X) with |α̲| = Σ_i i α_i. The Jordan type records more than the generic Jordan type of θ, since it also remembers the degrees of the kernels of the powers of θ.
items.note: The stratification on which the whole computation runs. Nothing in the atlas plans it; the classical analogue is the Jordan stratification of the nilpotent cone.

items.name: The groupoids of sheaves and of filtered sheaves
items.statement: Coh_ν(X) denotes the groupoid of coherent sheaves of class ν and Coh^{≥0}_ν(X) its full subgroupoid of sheaves in C_{≥0}. For ν̲ = (ν_1, …, ν_s), C̃oh_{ν̲}(X) is the groupoid of pairs (H, H_•) with H of class ν_1 + ⋯ + ν_s and H_1 ⊂ H_2 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ H_s = H a filtration with [H_i] = ν_1 + ⋯ + ν_i, and C̃oh^{≥0}_{ν̲}(X) its full subgroupoid of pairs with H ∈ C_{≥0}.
items.note: The stacks of filtered sheaves whose volumes are computed by the Hall algebra. GS.0 plans Bun_G and its level structures, not the stacks of filtered coherent sheaves.

items.name: The functors π_{α̲}, π′_{α̲} and π″_{α̲}
items.statement: There is a natural functor π_{α̲} : Nil_{α̲} → Coh_{α_1} × ⋯ × Coh_{α_s} sending (F,θ) to (F_1, …, F_s) with F_i = Ker(θ^i)/(Ker(θ^i) ∩ (Im θ + Ker θ^{i−1})) for i < s and F_s = F/Ker(θ^{s−1}). It factors as π_{α̲} = π″_{α̲} ∘ π′_{α̲} with π′_{α̲}(F,θ) = (H, H_•), H = F/Im θ and H_i = Ker(θ^i)/(Ker(θ^i) ∩ Im θ), and π″_{α̲}(H,H_•) = (H_1, H_2/H_1, …, H/H_{s−1}).
items.note: The factorisation that separates the filtration data from the nilpotent endomorphism.

items.name: Volumes of the fibres of π, π′ and π″
items.note: Proposition 3.1 and Corollary 3.2: the computation reducing the volume of the orbifold of nilpotent pairs to that of the stack of filtered sheaves, which the Hall algebra computes.

items.name: The Hall algebra of a curve
items.statement: For ν ∈ (Z²)^+ let I_ν = Obj(Coh_ν)/≅ and H_ν = Fun(I_ν, C). The convolution diagram Coh_{ν_1} × Coh_{ν_2} ←^p C̃oh_{ν_2,ν_1} →^s Coh_{ν_1+ν_2} induces m_{ν_1,ν_2}(f ⊗ g) = q^{½⟨ν_1,ν_2⟩} s_*p^*(f ⊠ g) and Δ′_{ν_1,ν_2}(h) = q^{½⟨ν_1,ν_2⟩} p_*s^*(h), valued in the completion H_{ν_1} ⊗̂ H_{ν_2} = Fun(I_{ν_1} × I_{ν_2}, C). Summing over ν gives an algebra and topological coalgebra H′ = ⊕_ν H_ν. With K = ⊕_{ν∈Z²} C k_ν the group algebra of Z², the extended Hall algebra is H = H′ ⊗ K for the action k_ν f k_{−ν} = q^{½(ν,α)}f on H_α, with Δ(k_ν) = k_ν ⊗ k_ν and Δ(f) = Σ_{ν_1+ν_2=ν} Δ′_{ν_1,ν_2}(f)·(k_{ν_2} ⊗ 1); by Green's theorem H is a topological bialgebra. The finitely supported part H^fin carries a symmetric Hopf pairing with (k_ν | k_μ) = q^{½(ν,μ)}, (1_F | 1_G) = δ_{F,G}/|Aut F| and (ab | c) = (a ⊗ b | Δ(c)).
items.note: The Ringel–Hall algebra of the category of coherent sheaves on a curve, with Green's theorem and the Hopf pairing. Nothing in the atlas plans Hall algebras in any form; the Tau Ceti quiver roadmap stops at Auslander–Reiten theory.

items.name: Characteristic functions and the basic volumes
items.statement: For ν ∈ (Z²)^+ let 1_ν, 1^vec_ν and 1^{≥0}_ν be the characteristic functions of Coh_ν, of the suborbifold Bun_ν of vector bundles, and of Coh^{≥0}_ν. Then (1_ν | 1_ν) = vol(Coh_ν), (1^vec_ν | 1^vec_ν) = vol(Bun_ν) and (1^{≥0}_ν | 1^{≥0}_ν) = vol(Coh^{≥0}_ν); for ν = (r,d) with r ≥ 1 one has 1_ν = Σ_{l≥0} q^{−l/2} 1^vec_{ν−(0,l)} 1_{0,l}. Moreover vol(C̃oh^{≥0}_{α̲}) = q^{−½Σ_{i>j}⟨α_i,α_j⟩}(1_{α_s}⋯1_{α_1} | 1^{≥0}_{Σα_i}).
items.note: The dictionary turning the volumes of Section 3 into Hall-algebra pairings; it is the step at which the problem becomes a computation with Eisenstein series.

items.name: Siegel's formula and the volumes of Bun and Coh
items.statement: (i) If ν = (r,d) with r > 0 then (1^vec_ν | 1^vec_ν) = (q^{(g−1)(r²−1)}/(q−1))·|Pic^0(X)|·ζ_X(q^{−2})⋯ζ_X(q^{−r}). (ii) Σ_{l≥0}(1_{0,l} | 1_{0,l})s^l = Exp(|X(F_q)|s/(q−1)) = ∏_{i=1}^∞ ζ_X(q^{−i}s). (iii) If ν = (r,d) with r > 0 then (1_ν | 1_ν) = (q^{(g−1)(r²−1)}/(q−1))·|Pic^0(X)|·∏_{i=2}^∞ ζ_X(q^{−i}). One writes vol_r = vol(Bun_{r,d}(X)), independent of d.
items.note: Statement (i) is Siegel's formula, i.e. the Tamagawa number one theorem for SL_r in the form of the volume of Bun_{r,d}; statement (ii) is the volume of the stack of torsion sheaves, proved in Appendix A from Heine's formula and the count of closed points by degree. GS.0 constructs Bun_G and its adelic description, and FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.2 the adeles and global Fourier analysis, but the volume formula itself is planned by neither.

items.name: Eisenstein series in the Hall algebra
items.statement: For r ≥ 0 set E_r(z) = Σ_{d∈Z} 1_{r,d} z^d and E^vec_r(z) = Σ_{d∈Z} 1^vec_{r,d} z^d, elements of ∏_d H_{r,d}, and E_{r_s,…,r_1}(z_s,…,z_1) = E_{r_s}(z_s)⋯E_{r_1}(z_1); by a theorem of Harder, the value of E_{r_s,…,r_1} on a coherent sheaf of rank r is the expansion in the region z_1 ≫ ⋯ ≫ z_s of a rational function.
items.note: Eisenstein series for GL_n over a function field, in their Hall-algebra incarnation. FA.6 plans automorphic forms on reductive groups over a function field with constant terms and cuspidal subspaces, but not the Hall-algebra Eisenstein series or Harder's rationality theorem.

items.name: The Hecke commutation relation
items.statement: (i) E_0(z)E_0(w) = E_0(w)E_0(z). (ii) For r ≥ 1, E_0(z)E^vec_r(w) = (∏_{i=0}^{r−1} ζ(q^{−r/2+i} z/w))·E^vec_r(w)E_0(z), where the rational function is expanded in the region w ≫ z.
items.note: The commutation relation between the torsion and vector-bundle Eisenstein series.

items.name: The coproduct of the Eisenstein series
items.note: The constant-term formula for the Eisenstein series, in coalgebra form.

items.name: The residue presentation of E^vec_r
items.note: The iterated residue that produces the higher-rank Eisenstein series out of the rank-one ones; it is the source of the operator Res_λ in the main formula.

items.name: Truncated Eisenstein series and the Harder–Narasimhan relations
items.statement: Put 1^{≥0}_{r,d} = 1_{Coh^{≥0}_{r,d}}, 1^{vec,≥0}_{r,d} = 1_{Bun^{≥0}_{r,d}} and 1^{<0}_{r,d} = 1_{Bun^{<0}_{r,d}}, and E^{≥0}_r(z), E^{vec,≥0}_r(z), E^{<0}_r(z) the corresponding series. Uniqueness of the Harder–Narasimhan filtration gives E_r(z) = Σ_{s+t=r} q^{½(g−1)st} E^{<0}_s(q^{t/2}z)E^{≥0}_t(q^{−s/2}z), and likewise for E^vec_r(z).
items.note: The truncation identities by which the counting series are separated from the full Eisenstein series.

items.name: The spherical Hall algebra and its integral form
items.statement: H^sph ⊆ H^fin is the subalgebra generated by K and the characteristic functions 1^vec_{1,d} and 1_{0,d} of the connected components of Pic(X) and of Coh_0(X); the characteristic function 1_{C_{α_1,…,α_t}} of every Harder–Narasimhan stratum belongs to it.
items.note: The spherical subalgebra, the analogue for a curve of the positive part of a quantum group in Ringel's theorem; it is what carries the genus-only, curve-independent structure.

items.name: The generic form of the spherical Hall algebra
items.statement: There exists an R_g-Hopf algebra _RH^sph with a Hopf pairing (,) : _RH^sph ⊗ _RH^sph → K_g, generated by elements _R1_{0,l} and _R1^vec_{1,d} for l ≥ 1 and d ∈ Z, containing elements _R1_{C_{α_1,…,α_t}} for every Harder–Narasimhan stratum, such that for every smooth connected projective curve X of genus g over a finite field there is a surjective specialisation morphism of Hopf algebras Ψ_X : _RH^sph ⊗_{R_g} C ↠ H_X^sph with Ψ_X(_R1_{C_{α_1,…,α_t}}) = 1_{C_{α_1,…,α_t}}.
items.locator: arXiv:1406.3839v2 (4 October 2014), Theorem 4.5, quoted from Schiffmann–Vasserot and Schiffmann
items.note: Due to Schiffmann–Vasserot and Schiffmann; it is the mechanism by which all the volumes become functions of the Weil numbers alone. It is quoted, not proved, here, and the two papers it rests on are listed as prerequisites.

items.name: Genus-only formulas for the volumes and the counts
items.statement: For every tuple α̲ = (α_1, …, α_s) there is an element B^{≥0}_{g,α̲} ∈ K_g with vol(C̃oh^{≥0}_{α̲}(X)) = B^{≥0}_{g,α̲}(σ_X) for every X; consequently there is C^{≥0}_{g,α} ∈ K_g with vol(Nil^{≥0}_α(X)) = C^{≥0}_{g,α}(σ_X), and then, by the plethystic relation of Section 2 and an induction on gcd(r,d), elements A^{≥0}_{g,α} and A_{g,α} ∈ K_g with A^{≥0}_α(X) = A^{≥0}_{g,α}(σ_X) and A_α(X) = A_{g,α}(σ_X) for every smooth projective curve X of genus g.
items.note: Corollaries 4.6 and 4.7: the existence half of Theorem 1.

items.name: Zariski density of the Weil numbers of curves of genus g
items.statement: Fix a prime l and an embedding ι : Q̄_l → C, and let X_g be the collection of all smooth projective geometrically connected curves of genus g defined over a finite field of characteristic different from l. Then W = {σ_X : X ∈ X_g} is Zariski dense in T_g/W_g.
items.locator: arXiv:1406.3839v2 (4 October 2014), Proposition 4.8, proved in Appendix B
items.note: Proposition 4.8, proved in Appendix B; it is exactly what gives the uniqueness half of Theorem 1, since it says that a polynomial identity valid on all curves of genus g is an identity in Q[T_g]^{W_g}. DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.0 owns Weil q-numbers and their properties but plans no density statement of this kind.

items.name: The generating series G^{≥0} and A^*
items.statement: Put G^{≥0}_{r_s,…,r_1}(z_s,…,z_1;w) = (E_{r_s,…,r_1}(z_s,…,z_1) | E^{≥0}_n(w)) with n = Σ_i r_i, an element of K_g[[z_s/z_{s−1}, …, z_2/z_1, z_1, w]] which is the expansion of a rational function; and A^*_{r_s,…,r_1}(z_s,…,z_1;w) = (E^vec_{r_s,…,r_1}(z_s,…,z_1) | E^*_r(w)) for * empty, ≥0 or <0. The coefficient of z_s^{d_s}⋯z_1^{d_1}w^d is (1_{r_s,d_s}⋯1_{r_1,d_1} | 1^*_{r,d}), nonzero only if d = Σ_i d_i.
items.note: The generating series that carry the computation of Theorem 2.

items.name: Separating the torsion factor
items.note: Proposition 5.1: the torsion part of the Eisenstein series contributes an explicit plethystic factor.

items.name: The untruncated series
items.statement: Assume r_i ≥ 1 for all i. Then A_{r̲}(z̲;w) = q^{½(g−1)Σ_{i>j} r_i r_j} ∏_i vol_{r_i} · ∏_i {Σ_{l∈Z} z_i^l w^l q^{½l(r_{<i} − r_{>i})}}.
items.note: Lemma 5.2: the easy case, from which the truncated ones are obtained by an induction.

items.name: Shuffle formulas for the truncated series in rank one
items.note: Proposition 5.3: the shuffle presentation of the truncated Eisenstein pairings, and the origin of the symmetrising kernel L(z_n,…,z_1) in Theorem 2.

items.name: A separation lemma for expansions in different regions
items.statement: Let K_g[z_s^{±1},…,z_1^{±1}]_loc be the localization at the linear polynomials z_i − c z_j, and for γ ∈ S_s let τ_γ be the expansion map into K_g[[z_s^{±1},…,z_1^{±1}]] in the region U_γ = {z_{γ(1)} ≫ ⋯ ≫ z_{γ(s)}}. If elements f_γ of the localization satisfy Σ_γ τ_γ(f_γ) = 0, then Σ_γ f_γ = 0.
items.note: The formal lemma that lets identities proved region by region be assembled.

items.name: A plethystic product identity
items.statement: Exp((|X(F_q)|/(q−1))[Σ_{i,l≥1} q^{−r_{[i,i+l]}}(q^{r_{i+l}} − 1)z^l]) = ∏_{s ∈ λ^∘} ζ_X(q^{−1−l(s)} z^{a(s)}), where λ^∘ denotes the boxes of λ outside the first column.
items.note: Lemma 5.5: the identity that converts the plethystic factor into the product J_λ(z) over the boxes of a Young diagram.

items.name: Strong generation and quot schemes
items.statement: A vector bundle F is strongly generated by a vector bundle G if Ext^1(G,F) = 0 and the canonical map G ⊗ Hom(G,F) → F is surjective; then dim Hom(G,F) = ⟨G,F⟩. For a vector bundle V and α = (r,d), the quot scheme Quot(V, α) represents the functor assigning to an affine k-scheme S the set of equivalence classes of epimorphisms V ⊠ O_S ↠ F with F an S-flat coherent sheaf on X × S whose fibres have rank r and degree d, two epimorphisms being equivalent when they have the same kernel. It is a projective, generally singular scheme, and the tangent space at φ : V ↠ F is Hom(Ker φ, F). Choosing a line bundle L of sufficiently negative degree so that Ker φ is strongly generated by L, and setting a = ⟨L,V⟩ and b = ⟨L, V − α⟩, the map sending φ to Hom(L, Ker φ) ⊆ Hom(L,V) ≅ k^a is a closed embedding Quot(V,α) → Gr(a,b).
items.note: AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.2 constructs the Hilbert and Quot schemes with a fixed Hilbert polynomial, proves representability and projectivity in the applicable range, and includes the boundedness argument realising the functor inside a Grassmannian; the tangent-space description and the strong-generation condition are part of that package.

items.name: A good pair of line bundles
items.statement: There is a pair of line bundles (L_1, L_2) ∈ Pic^{−n}(X) × Pic^{−m}(X) such that (a) every semistable Higgs bundle of class α is strongly generated by L_1 and by L_2; (b) every indecomposable vector bundle of class α is strongly generated by L_1 and by L_2; (c) for every coherent sheaf V of class α and every epimorphism φ : L_1 ⊗ V′ ↠ V, Ker(φ) is strongly generated by L_2; (d) every unstable Higgs sheaf of class α has a destabilizing Higgs subsheaf strongly generated by L_1 and L_2.
items.note: Lemma 6.1: the boundedness input that makes the two-line-bundle quot construction of Álvarez-Cónsul and King work here.

items.name: The two-line-bundle quot presentation and the Kronecker quiver
items.statement: With l_i = ⟨L_i, α⟩ and V_i = k^{l_i}, consider Q_{L_1,L_2} = Quot((L_1⊗V_1) ⊕ (L_2⊗V_2), α) and its open subscheme Q^{∘,∘}_{L_1,L_2} where both φ_{i*} : V_i → Hom(L_i, F) are isomorphisms, which is smooth and carries an action of G = GL(V_1) × GL(V_2) with [Q^{∘,∘}_{L_1,L_2}/G] ≅ Coh^{>L_1}_{r,d}(X). The cotangent space at φ is Hom(Ker φ, F)^*, the moment map μ : T^*Q^{∘,∘}_{L_1,L_2} → g^* factors as ν_φ ∘ κ_φ through the long exact sequence of the presentation, and [μ^{−1}(0)/G] ≅ Higgs^{>L_1}_{r,d}(X), an open substack containing Higgs^st_{r,d}(X). Setting h = dim Hom(L_2, L_1), V = Hom(L_2,L_1) and E = Hom(V_1 ⊗ V, V_2), the representation space of the Kronecker quiver with h arrows, there is an embedding j : Q^{∘,∘}_{L_1,L_2} → E as a smooth locally closed subvariety, and T^*E is the representation space of the doubled Kronecker quiver with moment map μ(x̲, y̲) = (Σ_i y_i x_i, −Σ_i x_i y_i). Let P be the Zariski closure of Q^{∘,∘}_{L_1,L_2} in E.
items.note: The local presentation of the stacks Coh_{r,d} and Higgs_{r,d} by quot schemes and by a Kronecker quiver, following Álvarez-Cónsul and King; it is what transports Crawley-Boevey and Van den Bergh's quiver argument to curves. R09.2 supplies the quot schemes and R09.4 the algebraic stacks, but this presentation is the paper's own.

items.name: King stability for the doubled Kronecker quiver
items.statement: For the character γ : G → k^*, (g_1,g_2) ↦ det(g_1)^{l_2} det(g_2)^{−l_1}: (i) a point (x̲, y̲) ∈ T^*E is γ-semistable (resp. γ-stable) if and only if every subrepresentation W = (W_1, W_2) satisfies l_1 dim(W_2) − l_2 dim(W_1) ≥ 0 (resp. > 0); (ii) the same criterion holds on T^*P, where a subrepresentation is a pair (W_1, W_2) with x_i(W_1) ⊆ W_2 and y_i ∈ p_W/(T_x P)^⊥.
items.note: Lemma 6.2, King's numerical criterion in the form needed here. Nothing in the atlas plans geometric invariant theory for quiver representations; the Tau Ceti quiver roadmap stops before stability and moduli.

items.name: Semistable points lie in the smooth locus
items.note: Lemma 6.3: the semistable locus of the possibly singular closure lies in the smooth open part.

items.name: Indecomposability as a condition on the moment map
items.statement: Assume r and d coprime, choose n, m so that l_1 and l_2 are also coprime, let λ ∈ g^* be λ(u_1,u_2) = l_2 Tr(u_1) − l_1 Tr(u_2), and assume p > l_1 l_2. Then λ(Id,Id) = 0 and λ(e_1,e_2) ≠ 0 for every nontrivial pair of projectors. For a k-point φ : (L_1⊗V_1) ⊕ (L_2⊗V_2) ↠ F of Q^{∘,∘}_{L_1,L_2} one has kλ ⊆ Im(μ_φ) if and only if F is indecomposable.
items.note: Lemma 6.4, the heart of Section 6 and the reason for the two-line-bundle presentation: the non-zero fibres of the moment map over the line kλ see exactly the indecomposable sheaves. It is the direct analogue of Crawley-Boevey and Van den Bergh's argument for quivers, and the explicit characteristic bound p > l_1l_2 is where the constant C(r,d) of Theorem 3 comes from.

items.name: The deformation Y → A of the stable Higgs moduli space
items.statement: Put A = kλ ⊆ g^*, X = μ^{−1}(A) ⊆ T^*P, X_t = μ^{−1}({tλ}) and X′ = X ∖ X_0. Since μ is G-equivariant it descends to μ̄ : (T^*P)^{ss} // G → A; set Y = μ̄^{−1}(A), Y_t = μ̄^{−1}({tλ}) and Y′ = Y ∖ Y_0, so that Y = X^{ss} // G with X^{ss} = X ∩ (T^*P)^{ss} ⊆ T^*Q^{∘,∘}_{L_1,L_2}.
items.note: The smooth family over the affine line whose special fibre is the moduli space of stable Higgs bundles and whose other fibres see the indecomposable bundles.

items.name: Smoothness of the deformation and its special fibre
items.statement: The k-schemes Y, Y′ and Y_t for t ∈ k are smooth, and X′ ⊆ X^{ss}. Moreover there is a canonical isomorphism of schemes Y_0 ≅ Higgs^st_{r,d}(X).
items.note: Lemma 6.5 and Proposition 6.6. The identification of the special fibre with the stable Higgs moduli space uses the translation between destabilizing Higgs subsheaves and destabilizing subrepresentations of the Kronecker quiver, with the tightness argument of Álvarez-Cónsul and King.

items.name: Destabilizing subsheaves and destabilizing subrepresentations
items.statement: With ψ the map sending a subsheaf to the corresponding pair of subspaces: W ∈ S′_X if and only if ψ(W) ∈ S′_{Kr}, i.e. ψ^{−1}(S′_{Kr}) = S′_X; and for W ∈ S_X with (W_1,W_2) = ψ(W), one has μ(W) > μ(α) if and only if l_1 dim(W_2) < l_2 dim(W_1).
items.note: Lemmas 6.7 and 6.8, the dictionary between Higgs stability on the curve and King stability for the quiver.

items.name: The contracting G_m-action and the equality of point counts
items.statement: The G_m-action z·(x̲, y̲) = (x̲, z y̲) descends to Y and is contracting: for every y ∈ Y the map z ↦ z·y extends to A^1 → Y. Let Z = Y^{G_m} = ⊔_i Z_i, a smooth subscheme of Y_0 (the moduli of chains on X), let n_i = dim T_z Y^+ for z ∈ Z_i and n′_i = n_i − 1 the corresponding integers for Y_0. The Bialynicki-Birula–Hesselink decompositions give Y = ⊔_i W_i and Y_0 = ⊔_i W′_i with W_i an A^{n_i}-fibration and W′_i an A^{n′_i}-fibration over Z_i, all defined over k. Hence |Y(k)| = |Y_0(k)| + (q−1)|Y_1(k)| and |Y(k)| = Σ_i q^{n_i}|Z_i(k)|, |Y_0(k)| = Σ_i q^{n_i−1}|Z_i(k)|, so |Y_0(k)| = |Y_1(k)|. Finally |Y_1(k)| = Σ_{F ∈ I_{r,d}} q^{dim Ext^1(F,F) − dim End(F) + 1} = q^{1−⟨α,α⟩}|I_{r,d}| = q^{1+(g−1)r²}|I_{r,d}|, which proves Theorem 3.
items.note: Proposition 6.9 and the conclusion of the proof of Theorem 3. The Bialynicki-Birula–Hesselink decomposition for a contracting G_m-action on a smooth variety is the geometric input; nothing in the atlas plans it.

items.name: Quasi-parabolic bundles and their counts
items.statement: Fix an effective divisor D = Σ_{i=1}^N p_i x_i with the x_i rational points of X. A quasi-parabolic vector bundle (V, F^•) on (X,D) is a vector bundle V with filtrations F^{(i)}_1 ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ F^{(i)}_{p_i} = V|_{x_i} for each i; the sequence of dimensions is the dimension type at x_i. For r > 0, d ∈ Z and fixed dimension types d^{(i)} = (d^{(i)}_1 ≤ ⋯ ≤ d^{(i)}_{p_i} = r), A_{r,d,d^{(1)},…,d^{(N)}}(X) is the number of geometrically indecomposable quasi-parabolic bundles on (X,D) of that rank, degree and dimension type, finite by the existence of Harder–Narasimhan filtrations.
items.note: GS.0 plans Bun_G with level structures, which is the parahoric analogue of a quasi-parabolic structure, but not the counting problem.

items.name: Theorem 4: the parabolic case
items.statement: For any fixed genus g, any N ≥ 0, any p = (p_1, …, p_N) and any tuple α = (r, d, d^{(1)}, …, d^{(N)}) with (r,d) ∈ N × Z and d^{(i)} = (d^{(i)}_1 ≤ ⋯ ≤ d^{(i)}_{p_i} = r), there exists a unique polynomial A_{g,p,α} ∈ Q[T_g]^{W_g} such that for every smooth projective curve X of genus g over a finite field and every divisor D = Σ_i p_i x_i with x_i ∈ X(F_q) one has A_α(X) = A_{g,p,α}(σ_X). For g = 0 this settles a conjecture of Schiffmann.
items.note: Theorem 4, proved along the same lines using the spherical Hall algebra of D-parabolic coherent sheaves. It answers, in the parabolic setting, a question of Deligne on counting irreducible l-adic local systems on a curve over a finite field.

items.name: Refinement by Harder–Narasimhan slope
items.statement: Fix g ≥ 0 and ν ∈ Q, and let A^{≥ν}_{r,d}(X), resp. A^{≤ν}_{r,d}(X), be the number of absolutely indecomposable vector bundles of class (r,d) lying in C_{≥ν}, resp. C_{≤ν}. Then there are polynomials A^{≥ν}_{g,r,d}, A^{≤ν}_{g,r,d} ∈ Q[T_g]^{W_g} with A^{≥ν}_{r,d}(X) = A^{≥ν}_{g,r,d}(σ_X) and A^{≤ν}_{r,d}(X) = A^{≤ν}_{g,r,d}(σ_X) for every smooth projective curve X of genus g over a finite field. When μ((r,d)) = ν this gives polynomials counting geometrically indecomposable semistable sheaves of slope ν.
items.note: Corollary 8.1, the refinement of Theorem 1 by slope.

items.name: Conjecture: polynomiality for each Harder–Narasimhan type
items.statement: Fix g ≥ 0. For every Harder–Narasimhan type (α_1, …, α_t) there is a polynomial A_{g,α_1,…,α_t} ∈ Q[T_g]^{W_g} such that the number A_{α_1,…,α_t}(X) of absolutely indecomposable vector bundles in C_{α_1,…,α_t} equals A_{g,α_1,…,α_t}(σ_X) for every smooth projective curve X of genus g over a finite field.
items.note: Conjecture 8.2, the natural strengthening of Corollary 8.1; a conjecture, not a theorem.

items.name: The spherical Hall Lie algebra of a curve
items.statement: Let X be a smooth projective curve of genus g over an algebraically closed field and let H^χ_ν be the space of C-valued constructible functions on Coh_ν; H^χ = ⊕_ν H^χ_ν is a cocommutative Hopf algebra, the χ-Hall algebra of X. Let H^{χ,sph} be the sub-Hopf-algebra generated by the constant functions on Coh_{0,d} and Bun_{1,l} for d ≥ 0 and l ∈ Z, an α_i = 1 limit of the spherical Hall algebra. The spherical Hall Lie algebra h^sph_X is the Lie algebra of primitive elements of H^{χ,sph}; it is conjectured to be independent of X with finite-dimensional Z²-graded components.
items.note: The proposed analogue for a curve of the Kac–Moody algebra of a quiver, built from the constructible-function Hall algebra of Lusztig and Joyce.

items.name: Conjectures: the analogues of Kac's conjecture and a Donaldson–Thomas identity
items.statement: (i) For every (r,d) ∈ (Z²)^+, A_{g,r,d}(0) = dim h^sph_{(r,d)}. (ii) Writing H^{sph,≥0}_ν for the subspace of H^sph_ν of functions supported on Coh^{≥0}_ν, so that H^{sph,≥0} is N²-graded with finite-dimensional components, Σ_ν dim(H^{sph,≥0}_ν) z^ν = Exp(Σ_ν A^{≥0}_{g,r,d}(0) z^ν) in N[[z^{(0,1)}, z^{(1,0)}]]. Both may be checked directly for g = 0 and g = 1.
items.note: Conjectures 8.3 and 8.4, the curve analogues of Kac's conjecture (proved for quivers by Hausel) and of a Donaldson–Thomas type identity; they are conjectures, and the remark that follows relates them to the K-theoretic and cohomological Hall algebras of the commuting variety of a genus-g curve.

items.name: Volume of the stack of torsion sheaves
items.statement: Let Coh^{(x)}_{0,d} be the suborbifold of torsion sheaves of degree d supported at a closed point x, with residue field k_x ≅ F_{q^{deg x}}. Then vol(Coh^{(x)}_{0,n deg x}) = |N_n(k_x)|/|GL_n(k_x)| = q^{n(n−1)deg x}/((q^{n deg x} − 1)⋯(q^{n deg x} − q^{(n−1)deg x})), and, using the factorisation over closed points, Heine's formula and Σ_{d|l} Σ_{deg x = d} d = |X(F_{q^l})|, one gets Σ_{d≥0}(1_{0,d} | 1_{0,d})s^d = exp(Σ_{l≥1} |X(F_{q^l})| s^l/(l(q^l − 1))) = Exp(|X(F_q)|s/(q−1)).
items.note: Appendix A, the proof of Theorem 4.1(ii). FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.5 constructs the Euler product of the zeta function by closed-point degree, which is the counting input; the volume of the stack of torsion sheaves is not planned.

prerequisites.citation: Victor Kac, Infinite root systems, representations of graphs and invariant theory, Invent. Math. 56 (1980), 57–92
prerequisites.why: The theorem that the number of geometrically indecomposable representations of a quiver of a given dimension vector over F_q is a polynomial in q, and the conjectures on its positivity and its constant term. This paper is the global analogue over a curve, and every one of its theorems and conjectures is patterned on a statement there.

prerequisites.citation: William Crawley-Boevey and Michel Van den Bergh, Absolutely indecomposable representations and Kac–Moody Lie algebras (with an appendix by Hiraku Nakajima), Invent. Math. 155 (2004), 537–559
prerequisites.why: The deformation argument relating absolutely indecomposable representations of a quiver to the points of a smooth quiver variety, by deforming the moment-map fibre along a line of characters. Section 6 of this paper is that argument transported to curves, and the constant C(r,d) comes from the analogue of their characteristic hypothesis.

prerequisites.citation: Olivier Schiffmann and Eric Vasserot, Hall algebras of curves, commuting varieties and Langlands duality, Math. Ann. 353 (2012), 1399–1451
prerequisites.why: The spherical Hall algebra of a smooth projective curve, its structure and its identification with the spherical part of a K-theoretic Hall algebra of the commuting variety; it is half of the generic-form theorem that the whole paper rests on.

prerequisites.citation: Olivier Schiffmann, Spherical Hall algebras of curves and Harder–Narasimhan strata, J. Korean Math. Soc. 48 (2011), no. 5, 953–967
prerequisites.why: The theorem that the characteristic function of every Harder–Narasimhan stratum lies in the spherical Hall algebra, and the construction of its integral form over R_g with the specialisation morphisms; it is the other half of the generic-form theorem, and it is what makes every volume in the paper a function of the Weil numbers alone.

prerequisites.citation: Mikhail Kapranov, Olivier Schiffmann and Eric Vasserot, The Hall algebra of a curve, Selecta Math. 23 (2017), 117–177
prerequisites.why: The structure of the Hall algebra of the category of coherent sheaves on a smooth projective curve — the product, the topological coproduct, Green's theorem and the Hopf pairing — which Section 4 recalls and uses throughout.

prerequisites.citation: Luis Álvarez-Cónsul and Alastair King, A functorial construction of moduli of sheaves, Invent. Math. 168 (2007), 613–666
prerequisites.why: The embedding of a quot scheme of sheaves presented by two line bundles into the representation space of a Kronecker quiver, and the comparison of sheaf stability with King stability through tight subrepresentations. Sections 6.4 to 6.7 are built on it.

prerequisites.citation: Alastair King, Moduli of representations of finite dimensional algebras, Quart. J. Math. Oxford 45 (1994), 515–530
prerequisites.why: Geometric invariant theory for representations of a quiver: the stability condition attached to a character and the numerical criterion in terms of subrepresentations, which is Lemma 6.2 here. The atlas plans no GIT for quiver representations.

prerequisites.citation: Michael Atiyah, On the Krull–Schmidt theorem with applications to sheaves, Bull. Soc. Math. France 84 (1956), 307–317
prerequisites.why: Krull–Schmidt for categories of coherent sheaves, with the local endomorphism rings of indecomposables; the Tau Ceti roadmap on quiver representations plans the theorem for finite-length modules over a finite-dimensional algebra, and this is the version Section 2 needs.

prerequisites.citation: Günter Harder, Chevalley groups over function fields and automorphic forms, Ann. of Math. 100 (1974), 249–306
prerequisites.why: The rationality of Eisenstein series over a function field: the value of E_{r_s,…,r_1}(z_s,…,z_1) on a coherent sheaf is the expansion of a rational function in the region z_1 ≫ ⋯ ≫ z_s. Every generating series in Sections 4 and 5 is manipulated as a rational function on the strength of it.

prerequisites.citation: Wim Hesselink, Concentration under actions of algebraic groups, Séminaire d'algèbre Paul Dubreil et M.-P. Malliavin (Paris, 1980), Lecture Notes in Math. 867, 55–89
prerequisites.why: The Bialynicki-Birula–Hesselink decomposition of a smooth variety with a contracting G_m-action into affine fibrations over the components of the fixed locus, which is what equates the point counts of the fibres of the deformation in Section 6.9.

prerequisites.citation: Tamás Hausel and Fernando Rodriguez-Villegas, Mixed Hodge polynomials of character varieties, Invent. Math. 174 (2008), 555–624
prerequisites.why: The conjectural formula for the mixed Hodge polynomial of the genus-g character variety for GL_r, to which Theorem 2 bears a strong similarity and from which it differs by the factors H_λ(z); the comparison is the main evidence discussed in the introduction.

prerequisites.citation: Tamás Hausel, Kac's conjecture from Nakajima quiver varieties, Invent. Math. 181 (2010), 21–37
prerequisites.why: The proof of Kac's conjecture that the constant term of the Kac polynomial of a quiver is the multiplicity of the corresponding root in the associated Kac–Moody algebra; Conjecture 8.3 is its curve analogue, and the paper's spherical Hall Lie algebra is the proposed substitute for the Kac–Moody algebra.

prerequisites.citation: Jiuzhao Hua, Counting indecomposable representations of quivers over finite fields, J. Algebra 226 (2000), 1011–1033
prerequisites.why: The generating-series formula for the Kac polynomials of a quiver, which the formula for the constant terms A_{g,r,d}(0) in Corollary 1.10 differs from only by an extra term −l(λ); it is the combinatorial model for the whole computation.

routes.title: Counting bundles over function fields: Hall algebras, Kac polynomials and Higgs moduli
routes.brief: Plan the counting of indecomposable vector bundles on a curve over a finite field, the Hall-algebra machinery that computes it, and its identification with the point count of the moduli space of stable Higgs bundles, after Schiffmann. The final theorems are his Theorems 1, 2, 3 and 4. Theorem 1: for each genus g and each (r,d) ∈ N × Z there is a unique element A_{g,r,d} of K_g, the localization of Q[T_g]^{W_g} at the multiplicative set generated by the q^l − 1, such that the number A_{r,d}(X) of geometrically indecomposable vector bundles of rank r and degree d on X equals A_{g,r,d}(σ_X) for every smooth projective geometrically connected curve X of genus g over a finite field, where σ_X ∈ T_g/W_g is the class of the Weil numbers of X. Theorem 2 makes it effective: with J_λ(z) = ∏_{s∈λ} ζ*_X(q^{−1−l(s)}z^{a(s)}) and H_λ(z) an iterated residue of an explicit symmetrising kernel L(z_n,…,z_1), the rational functions A_{g,r}(z) defined by Σ_{r≥1} A_{g,r}(z)T^r = (q−1)Log(Σ_λ q^{(g−1)⟨λ,λ⟩}J_λ(z)H_λ(z)T^{|λ|}) satisfy A_{g,r,d} = −Σ_{ξ∈μ_r} ξ^{−d} Res_{z=ξ}(A_{g,r}(z)dz/z). Theorem 3: for (r,d) coprime there is an explicit constant C(r,d) such that, whenever char(F_q) > C(r,d), |Higgs^st_{r,d}(X)(F_q)| = q^{1+(g−1)r²}·A_{r,d}(X). Theorem 4 is the same polynomiality for quasi-parabolic bundles along a fixed divisor. The roadmap must cover, in this order. (1) The arithmetic frame: the Weil numbers of a curve, the torus T_g with its W_g-action, the invariant ring R_g = Q[T_g]^{W_g} and its localization K_g, the class σ_X ∈ T_g/W_g, and the Zariski density of the set of such classes as X runs over all curves of genus g in a fixed residue characteristic — the density is what gives uniqueness in Theorem 1 and is routed separately as a source of DeligneWeightsAndPurity. (2) The categorical frame: classes and the Euler form ⟨(r,d),(r′,d′)⟩ = (1−g)rr′ + (rd′ − r′d) of a curve, slopes, semistable sheaves, Harder–Narasimhan filtrations and the categories C_ν, C_{α_1,…,α_t}, C_{≥ν} and C_{≤ν}, with their finiteness and base-change properties; Krull–Schmidt for coherent sheaves in the form of Atiyah's theorem, together with the computation of the radical of the endomorphism algebra of a decomposition and the ratio |End^nil(M)|/|Aut(M)| = ∏_i |k_{M_i}|^{n_i(n_i−1)}/|GL(n_i,k_{M_i})|; and geometric indecomposability. (3) The orbifold of pairs: the groupoids Nil_α(X) of pairs (F,θ) with θ a nilpotent endomorphism, their volumes, the finiteness of Nil^{≥0}_α(X), the plethystic identity Σ_α vol(Nil^{≥0}_α(X))z^α = Exp(Σ_α A^{≥0}_α(X)z^α/(q−1)), and the vanishing of the difference between A^{≥0}_{r,d} and A_{r,d} when d > (g−1)r(r−1). (4) The Jordan stratification: the Jordan type of a nilpotent pair, the stratification of Nil_α, the groupoids of filtered sheaves, the three functors π, π′, π″ and the volumes of their fibres, giving vol(Nil^{≥0}_{α̲}) = q^{d′(α̲)}vol(C̃oh^{≥0}_{α̲}). (5) The Hall algebra of a curve: the convolution product and coproduct on functions on the groupoids of coherent sheaves, the extended algebra with its group-algebra factor, Green's theorem, the Hopf pairing on the finitely supported part; the characteristic functions and their volumes, including Siegel's formula for vol(Bun_{r,d}) and the volume of the stack of torsion sheaves, both of which are routed separately as sources of GlobalShtukas; Eisenstein series E_r(z), E^vec_r(z) with Harder's rationality, the Hecke commutation relation, the coproduct formula, the residue presentation of E^vec_r, the truncated series and the Harder–Narasimhan relations among them; and the spherical subalgebra with its generic form over R_g, quoted from Schiffmann–Vasserot and Schiffmann, which is what makes every volume a function of σ_X alone. (6) The computation: the generating series G^{≥0} and A^*, the separation of the torsion factor, the untruncated series, the shuffle formulas for the rank-one truncated series, and the plethystic identity turning the answer into a product over the boxes of a Young diagram — and hence Theorem 2 and the companion formula for the constant terms A_{g,r,d}(0). (7) The Higgs side: Higgs sheaves and bundles with the canonical twist, their stability, the moduli stack and the smooth moduli space for coprime (r,d), the Hitchin map and the stable global nilpotent cone; the two-line-bundle quot presentation of Álvarez-Cónsul and King with its embedding into the representation space of a Kronecker quiver, King's stability criterion for the doubled quiver, the moment map, the criterion for indecomposability in terms of the line kλ, the smooth family Y → A^1 with Y_0 ≅ Higgs^st_{r,d}(X), the contracting G_m-action and the Bialynicki-Birula–Hesselink decomposition, and the resulting equality of point counts that proves Theorem 3; then the purity and Poincaré-polynomial corollaries over F_q and over C. (8) The extensions and the conjectures, recorded as conjectures and not as theorems: quasi-parabolic bundles and Theorem 4, the refinement by Harder–Narasimhan slope, the conjecture that A_{g,r,d} is independent of d (proved for r prime), the conjecture that each Harder–Narasimhan type has its own counting polynomial, the spherical Hall Lie algebra of a curve, and the two conjectures relating A_{g,r,d}(0) to its dimensions and to a Donaldson–Thomas identity. Import, and do not re-plan: the stack Bun_G on a global curve with its level structures, deformation complex, Harder–Narasimhan bounded opens, finite type and adelic description from Global shtukas and Langlands over function fields (GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands), stage GS.0, of which this paper is also a source; curves, function fields, adeles and the zeta function with its Euler product over closed points from Global function fields, reciprocity and automorphic foundations (FunctionFieldArithmetic), stages FA.0, FA.1, FA.2 and FA.5, and automorphic forms with constant terms and cuspidal subspaces from FA.6; Weil q-numbers, their weights and the functorial linear algebra of eigenvalues from Deligne weights, purity and the Weil bounds (DeligneWeightsAndPurity), stage DWP.0, of which this paper is also a source; the Hilbert and Quot schemes with their representability, projectivity, tangent spaces and Grassmannian embedding from Algebraic moduli and representability for arithmetic geometry (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry), stage R09.2, and algebraic stacks from R09.4; Higgs fields, the Hitchin base and map and the Picard stack acting on the fibres, for a reductive group over a curve over a finite field, from Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison), stage ET.2b, of which this paper is also a source; the Euler and Tits forms, dimension vectors, Krull–Schmidt for finite-length modules and Auslander–Reiten theory from the Tau Ceti roadmap on quiver representations, which is existing work and is never re-planned. Young diagrams, the conjugate partition and partitions are in Mathlib (YoungDiagram, YoungDiagram.transpose, Nat.Partition) and must not be rebuilt; nothing else in this roadmap is in the libraries. The roadmap owns, and must plan itself: the counting functions and their polynomiality, the orbifold of pairs and the Jordan stratification, the Hall algebra of a curve with its spherical subalgebra and generic form, the plethystic calculus, the explicit formulas, and the whole deformation argument relating indecomposable bundles to stable Higgs bundles. The conjectures of Sections 1 and 8 are to be stated with their exact hypotheses and recorded as open.
routes.reason: Nothing in the atlas goes in this direction. The subject is the enumeration of indecomposable vector bundles on a curve over a finite field, the Hall algebra of the category of coherent sheaves on that curve with its spherical subalgebra and its generic form, and the comparison of the answer with the point count of the moduli space of stable Higgs bundles. Searches of the layer descriptions return no occurrence of 'Hall algebra', of 'Kac polynomial', of 'character variety', of 'nilpotent cone' in this sense, or of any counting problem for bundles. What the atlas does have are the two ends of the story and neither of its middles: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.0 constructs Bun_G on a global curve with its Harder–Narasimhan bounded opens and adelic description, and EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.2b constructs the Hitchin base and map with the Picard stack acting on its fibres, for a reductive group over a curve over a finite field, as machinery for Ngô's proof of the fundamental lemma. Neither roadmap heads towards counting, and the mathematics between them — Hall algebras, Eisenstein series in Hall-algebra form, the orbifold of nilpotent pairs, the plethystic calculus, the two-line-bundle quot presentation and the deformation of the Higgs moduli space — belongs to neither. It is not a Part II of GS, because GS is organised around shtukas and the Langlands correspondence and this work uses only its first layer; it is not a Part II of ET, because ET is organised around the trace formula and this work uses only its Hitchin geometry. The closest existing direction is the Tau Ceti roadmap on quiver representations, whose Euler form, Krull–Schmidt theorem and Auslander–Reiten theory are the exact local model for Sections 2 and 6 of this paper; but a Tau Ceti roadmap is existing work that is never re-planned, and what this paper does is not an extension of quiver theory but its global analogue over a curve. So a new roadmap, in the function-fields galaxy alongside FunctionFieldArithmetic and GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands, which it imports from.

GS.0 constructs Bun_G on the global curve with its level structures, deformation complex and Harder–Narasimhan bounded opens, proves that the relevant bounded opens are of finite type, accounts for automorphisms and central degree, and gives the adelic description of rational points; its acceptance examples are GL_1 giving the Picard stack and GL_n with unstable bundles showing that Bun_G is not a finite-type proper scheme. Two statements the layer needs and does not plan are proved here. The first is Siegel's formula in the shape (1^vec_{r,d} | 1^vec_{r,d}) = (q^{(g−1)(r²−1)}/(q−1))·|Pic^0(X)|·ζ_X(q^{−2})⋯ζ_X(q^{−r}), the volume of Bun_{r,d} over a finite field, together with the companion formula for the volume of the whole stack of coherent sheaves; this is the Tamagawa-number statement for SL_r in stack-volume form, and it is exactly the quantitative content that GS.0's finite-type statements leave open. The second is the volume of the stack of torsion sheaves, Σ_{l≥0}(1_{0,l} | 1_{0,l})s^l = Exp(|X(F_q)|s/(q−1)) = ∏_{i≥1} ζ_X(q^{−i}s), proved in the paper's Appendix A from the factorisation over closed points, the count |N_n(k)| = |k|^{n(n−1)} of the nilpotent cone and Heine's formula. The route also names the Euler form and Harder–Narasimhan package of Section 2.1, which GS.0 plans and for which this paper is a clean written source in the GL_r case.

DWP.0 defines Weil q-numbers on actual algebraic-number carriers with their all-embeddings absolute-value property, proves independence of a splitting field, uniqueness of weight, and the behaviour under products, duals, Tate twists and finite-field base extension. The statement proved in this paper's Appendix B is of the same kind and is not planned there: fixing a prime l and an embedding of Q̄_l into C, the set of classes σ_X ∈ T_g/W_g of the Weil numbers of smooth projective geometrically connected curves of genus g over finite fields of characteristic different from l is Zariski dense in T_g/W_g. It is a statement about which tuples of Weil numbers actually occur, and it is what turns 'the same formula holds for every curve of genus g' into an identity of elements of Q[T_g]^{W_g} — the uniqueness half of the paper's first theorem. Any later roadmap that wants to define an invariant by its values on all curves of a fixed genus needs it.

ET.2b constructs, for a smooth proper curve over a finite field and a reductive group scheme in the source's good-characteristic range, the stack of G-bundles, Higgs fields twisted by a chosen sufficiently positive divisor, the Hitchin base and map, cameral and spectral covers and the Picard stack acting on the Hitchin fibres, and proves algebraicity and finite-type bounds. The boundedness statement proved here is of that kind and is not planned: there is a pair of line bundles (L_1, L_2) on X such that every semistable Higgs bundle and every indecomposable vector bundle of a fixed class is strongly generated by each of them, every kernel of an epimorphism from L_1 ⊗ V is strongly generated by L_2, and every unstable Higgs sheaf has a destabilizing Higgs subsheaf strongly generated by both. It is the input that makes a quot-scheme presentation of the Higgs stack possible at all, and it is stated for the canonical twist rather than for a sufficiently positive one. The route also names the definitions of Higgs sheaves and of the stable moduli space, which ET.2b plans for a general reductive group and for which this paper is a source in the GL_r case with the canonical twist and the coprime stability condition.
